evals.query: Here's the trip summary screen from our travel planner's iPhone app (HTML attached). It feels messy. Can you make it look better? Send back the improved HTML.
expected_behavior: Chooses one focal point for the screen and says what it is.
Reduces the competing emphasis so there is one primary action, with the other actions visibly secondary instead of four equally loud coloured buttons.
Replaces the mixed padding and margin values with a consistent spacing scale (for example multiples of 4 or 8) and applies it in the code.
Fixes the low-contrast grey text with specific colour values that meet contrast for their size.
Returns complete revised HTML that keeps every piece of content and every action from the original.
States plainly whether the result was rendered and looked at, and names what still needs checking (for example dark mode or larger text sizes).

evals.query: We're bringing our podcast player to the Mac. Design the Settings window: Playback (skip back and forward intervals, playback speed, continuous play), Downloads (auto-download new episodes, storage limit, download location), Notifications (new episodes, per show), and Account (signed-in email, sign out, delete account). Give me SwiftUI and explain the layout.
expected_behavior: Uses the macOS settings conventions (a Settings scene with a toolbar tab per section) rather than an iPhone-style navigation list.
Lays out each pane as a form with labels and controls aligned in consistent columns and spacing.
Picks native controls that fit each setting (for example pop-up menus for intervals, a folder picker for the download location, checkboxes or toggles for on and off) with sensible defaults.
Separates the destructive account actions from the rest and asks for confirmation before deleting the account.
Addresses the window size across panes (a fixed width, or pane heights that adapt) instead of leaving it to chance.
Provides SwiftUI code using real APIs, with a short explanation of the layout choices.
